about: Every construction assumption in one table. Nobody measured these walls. The values are typical for 1990s North American suburban houses. loss_db is the loss for one pass through the item, per band. reflection (0 to 1) is the share of wave amplitude that bounces off in the wave animation. Edit a number and reload the page. The calibration step then moves loss_db toward what the samples show; these numbers are its starting point.

pathLoss.about: Log-distance model. pl0_db is the loss at 1 m: the free-space value (40.2 dB at 2.4 GHz, 46.9 dB at 5 GHz) plus 6 dB for the small antennas of sensors and phones. n is the path-loss exponent before walls are counted.

ext-siding.label: Exterior wall: wood frame, sheathing, vinyl siding
ext-siding.note: Aluminium siding or foil-faced sheathing would lose 15 dB or more. Brick veneer: use ext-brick.

ext-brick.label: Exterior wall: wood frame with brick veneer
ext-brick.note: Common on the front of 1990s suburban houses. Not used until you assign it to a wall.

int-drywall.label: Interior wall: wood studs, drywall both sides

int-garage.label: Garage-to-house wall: insulated studs, fire-rated drywall

glass-lowe.label: Low-E double-glazed window
glass-lowe.note: The metal-oxide coating reflects radio. Published values run from 5 to 30 dB. Clear double glazing is about 3 dB.

door-exterior.label: Exterior or garage-entry door: insulated steel or fibreglass (closed)

masonry.label: Brick fireplace and chimney
masonry.note: Used for fixtures. The loss is for a path through the whole fixture.

appliance-metal.label: Large metal appliance (range, washer, furnace)
appliance-metal.note: Used for fixtures. The loss is for a path through the whole fixture.

cabinetry.label: Counters and cabinets
cabinetry.note: Used for fixtures. The loss is for a path through the whole fixture.

floor-wood.label: Wood-joist floor with subfloor and drywall ceiling

construction.about: Which material the floor-plan importer (tools/trace/import_polycam.py) gives to each kind of wall, window and door. Every entry is an assumption: a LiDAR scan measures where a wall is, not what it is made of. Polycam also draws every wall 0.10 m thick (a drawing setting, not a measurement), so the thickness of a wall comes from its material above.
construction.doorStateNote: Interior doors were open during the scan and are modelled open. Exterior, garage and garage-entry doors are modelled closed.
construction.closeOuterWallGapsNote: Where the scan left a stretch of the outer edge of a level without a wall, the importer adds an exterior wall there and marks it. A house has no hole in its outer wall; the gap is where the scanner could not see.

defaults.about: Ceiling heights are assumed (8 ft upper floor, 9 ft main floor). Access points and sensors are assumed to sit 1 m above the floor unless a position gives z.
